title: Sandiganbayan affirms grant of bail to Revilla
summary: The Sandiganbayan Third Division has upheld its granting of bail to former senator Ramon Revilla Jr. in his malversation case involving an alleged ghost flood control project in Pandi, Bulacan.

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Sandiganbayan Third Division has upheld its granting of bail to former senator Ramon Revilla Jr. in his malversation case involving an alleged ghost flood control project in Pandi, Bulacan.
In a 49-page resolution, the anti-graft court denied the prosecution’s motion for reconsideration that sought to overturn the grant of bail to Revilla while the case is undergoing trial.

The court also denied the motions of former public works officials Brice Hernandez, Arjay Domasig, Jaypee Mendoza, Juanito Mendoza, Emelita Juat and Christina Pineda to reconsider the denial of their bail petitions.

The anti-graft court maintained that the funds involved in the case are not public in nature as far as Revilla is concerned. It said the boxes of cash allegedly received by him supposedly came from a pool of funds coming from contributions of private contractors.

It said that even if it were to be assumed that the prosecution had managed to present strong evidence of guilt that the former senator may have received cash from private contractors, it would only prove the existence of bribery, which is a bailable offense, and not malversation due to the private nature of the funds.

The Sandiganbayan also said the prosecution was not able to prove that there was conspiracy on the part of Revilla as it alleged that Revilla facilitated the funding for the project when it was included in the national budget.
It ruled that Revilla’s participation in the legislative process was diluted and attenuated.
Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla had slammed the original grant of bail, saying the issue appeared to have been “natrabaho.”
There was no comment from the two associate justices who approved the bail – Ronald Moreno and Fritz Bryn Anthony delos Santos. Third Division chairman Karl Miranda had voted to deny the bail.
